The recursive scan for getting the subject structure is core to understanding how 
the lesson retrieval system works. As mentioned in 4.6 Database Design, the S3 
database contains subject objects, which contain 0..* topic, that hold 0..* 
subtopics, and finally they contain 0..* lessons. Each of these objects hold a file 
called metadata.json, this file contains the objects name that should be 
displayed to the user. The S3 handler, will perform a depth first search on this 
data structure, for a given subject, and will intern create class structure as 
described in Figure 37. To further bolster the performance of the download, a 
countdown latch maybe utilised, enabling multiple requests to be made at once, 
with finally awaiting the latch at the end to ensure the entire data structure is 
complete.  
To display the content, RecyclerViews will be utilised, with the topic being the 
parent object and the lessons and subtopics being the children in a nested 
format. This structure enables for efficient scrolling, thereby enhancing 
performance and resource utilisation.
